articleTitle: A Convolutional Knowledge Tracking Model with Forgetting Behavior and Graph Embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: With the prevalence of various intelligent educational systems, it is imperative to uncover learners' proficiency in mastering knowledge points through their prior practice circumstances. Knowledge tracking is an extremely beneficial instrument in this regard. Among them, Convolutional Knowledge Tracking (CKT) has demonstrated excellent performance in numerous KT tasks, while it does not take into account the phenomenon of forgetting and the interconnection between knowledge points. In order to tackle these problems, we propose a model called FGE-CKT, which integrates forgetting behavior and graph embedding with CKT. Our model addresses the drawbacks of forgetting characteristics by modelling three key factors affecting students' forgetting behaviors through a fully connected neural net: repeated knowledge learning times, adjacent learning interval and interval between visits to repeat knowledge. At the same time, convolutional neural networks are used to simultaneously extract and incorporate connections between knowledge points into the model's input portion. It was confirmed by experiments on two well-established datasets that FGE-CKT achieved significant improvements in AUC performance.

articleTitle: Cross-band broadband waveguide cavity duplexer design
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In this paper, a waveguide cavity duplexer spanning the X and Ku bands operates in the upstream band of satellite signals. Compared with the general duplexer, the T-junction of the broadband ridge waveguide is designed, and the high mode of the low-end channel is suppressed, and the two-way synthesis across the octave is realized. The duplexer is mainly composed of rectangular waveguide-spine waveguide transition, ridge waveguide filter, ridge waveguide T-junction and waveguide H mask filter. The modeling simulation optimization is performed with HFSS, and the results show that the return loss is greater than 25dB in the 7.9GHz-8.4GHz frequency band and greater than 25dB in the 14GHz-14.5GHz frequency band.

articleTitle: A traffic accident prediction model based on a Spatial-Attention Temporal Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Traffic accidents often result in significant casualties and economic losses. Accurate and timely prediction of traffic accidents is crucial for public safety and reducing economic impact. However, predicting traffic accidents is challenging due to their complex causes, involving spatial, temporal dynamics, and external influences within heterogeneous traffic-related data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a Spatial-Attention Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (SATGCN) for predicting traffic accidents. In the process of predicting traffic accidents, at the first stage, the spatial convolution layer leverages GCN and attention mechanisms to extract spatial features. Then, the temporal convolution layer extracts spatiotemporal features through stacked spatiotemporal modules, followed by dimensionality reduction via average pooling. Finally, the processed spatial, temporal, and external features are fused and passed through a fully connected layer to generate the prediction result. The simulation demonstrated that the model performed better than the baseline on the Beijing Traffic Accident Dataset, with its precision improved by 5% compared to DSTGCN.

articleTitle: Coupling-Induced Capacity Analysis of Holographic MIMO Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In recent years, the multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) technology has emerged as a focal point, due to the escalating demands for increased communication capacity. Holographic multiple-input-multiple-output (HMIMO), which aims to use dense antenna arrays to record and reconstruct the amplitude and phase of EM wavefronts, offers significant potential for the enhancement of the spectral efficiency. However, in HMIMO system, since the spacing between the array elements is significantly reduced (i.e., << λ/2), the mutual coupling between them is inevitable, which needs to be taken into consideration when evaluating the system performance. In this paper, the impact of mutual coupling on antenna radiation efficiency for both 1D linear antenna array and 2D surface array is investigated. Then, the capacity gain of a HMIMO system, taking into account the influence of coupling, is analyzed. Results show that, if the number of receive antenna elements is fixed, for a linear array, HMIMO communication systems cannot provide capacity gains. For a surface array, the capacity of HMIMO system is 2~3 bps/Hz lower than that of MIMO system.

articleTitle: Adaptive Parallel Optimization Design for Signal Processing on Multi-core and Many-core Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Based on the characteristics and parallel design research of multi-core and many-core hardware platforms, this paper proposes an adaptive parallel optimization design method for signal processing on multi-core and many-core platforms. By employing a hardware platform architecture-aware approach and a multi-core segmented pipeline design, adaptive parallel optimization is achieved. The method was tested and verified using a two-stage FFT algorithm on the Phytium 2000+ platform. The test results indicate that through multiple iterations of optimization, adaptive high-performance parallel processing on multi-core and many-core platforms can be realized.

articleTitle: MQTT-Based Internet of Things Smart Home Linkage Control System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The core architecture of the system designed in this paper is based on STM32 micro-controller, integrated with DHT11 temperature and humidity sensor, BH1750 light intensity detector and other components, and utilizes the integrated Wi-Fi module of ESP8266 to communicate with AliCloud IoT platform. The system uses the MQTT protocol to send data to the platform, and through the developed WeChat applet, combined with AliCloud's cloud product streaming function, the data is transmitted to the mobile terminal to realize the remote data storage function. In addition, the system also embeds the SG90 servo drive unit as an analog component of the robotic arm operating system, and collaborates with the ESP32-CAM remote video monitoring device to realize all-round detection and control, providing convenience for people's lives.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Principle of Ambiguity Function in Linear Canonical Transform Domain
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The ambiguity function (AF) and its related uncertainty function are essential time-frequency analysis method for the waveform properties and echo-location in radar and optical applications. This paper devotes to investigate new uncertainty principles of AF in linear canonical transform domain (AFL) for complex-value function. Firstly, the moments of AFL are defined to measure mean and the covariance of signal in time and frequency domain. Then new uncertainty principles of AFL are proposed related to moments, which capture lower bounds for product of time delay and Doppler spreads. The lower bound can be only achieved by Gaussian-type function. Furthermore, an example with Gaussian-type function is performed to verify the correctness of proposed uncertainty principles. Finally, potential applications of derived theorems are explored in the field of radar.

articleTitle: Impact of Phase Noise and Dispersion on OFDM Transmission Performance and the Improvement Effects of Pilot Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In modern communication systems, phase noise and dispersion are critical factors that significantly affect the quality of signal transmission. This paper delves into a comprehensive analysis of the impact of phase noise and dispersion on transmission performance, with a particular focus on the bit error rate (BER) performance of various modulation schemes, including Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK), Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK), and 16-level Quadrature Amplitude Modulation (16-QAM). The study meticulously compares the BER performance of these modulation schemes before and after the removal of dispersion, highlighting the importance of effective dispersion management in modern communication systems. Furthermore, the paper explores the enhancement effects of incorporating pilot techniques to mitigate phase noise. This is achieved by varying the pilot signal lengths and insertion intervals, aiming to optimize the overall system performance. To validate the theoretical analysis, a series of MATLAB simulation experiments are conducted, providing empirical evidence to support the findings. The results underscore the critical role of dispersion removal and pilot techniques in improving transmission quality, offering valuable insights for the design and optimization of robust communication systems.

articleTitle: Improvement Scheme of VSLAM System in Dynamic Map Point Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Precision localization and mapping within indoor environments represent a significant challenge for Visual Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (VSLAM) systems. While existing methodologies, such as ORB-SLAM3, demonstrate high accuracy in static settings, their capacity for precise localization and robustness is substantially compromised in the presence of dynamic objects. Consequently, mitigating the impact of dynamic objects on the localization and mapping processes of VSLAM systems is an imperative issue that demands immediate resolution. To address this challenge, this paper introduces an enhanced ORB-SLAM3 approach that integrates deep learning with dynamic environment mitigation, tailored specifically for indoor settings characterized by motion. By amalgamating the state-of-the-art YOLOv10 object detection algorithm with the Lucas-Kanade (LK) optical flow technique to eliminate dynamic map points, the proposed algorithm effectively neutralizes the influence of dynamic objects on pose estimation, thereby bolstering the robustness of VSLAM systems in the context of dynamic scene localization. Empirical findings indicate that, in comparison to the original ORB-SLAM3, the refined algorithm has realized a marked enhancement of over 95% in Average Trajectory Error (ATE) within highly dynamic environments, with improvements in Relative Trajectory Error (RTE) also exceeding 95%, without compromising the system's operational real-time integrity.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency LC-MSNN Prototype with Integrated Bipolar Signaling and Half-Cycle Delayed Gating
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This study introduces a hardware prototype for the Locally Connected Memristor Spiking Neural Network (LC-MSNN), showcasing a high level of energy efficiency and system integration. The prototype integrates bipolar signaling and employs half-cycle delayed gating mechanisms, which are critical for accurate signal processing in neuromorphic computing. The circuit design is meticulously optimized for chip integration and response velocity, featuring a small signal channel and a drive mode channel that facilitate the generation of unipolar and bipolar pulses, respectively. The architecture supports independent neuron operation while ensuring functional interconnectivity, aligning with the operational dynamics of biological neural networks. Notably, when benchmarked on the MNIST dataset, the prototype achieved a recognition rate of 95.2% with a power consumption of only 2.5mW, demonstrating its effectiveness in practical applications.

articleTitle: Heart Sound Classification Based on Features of FBPSI
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Cardiovascular disease triggers abnormal changes in the structure and function of the heart, leading to a decrease in the heart’s contraction and pumping ability, which seriously threatens the life and health of patients. Therefore, we propose a heart sound analysis method with frequency-balanced power spectral intensity characteristics to effectively distinguish normal and pathological heart sound signals. First, the heart sound signals were denoised and normalized to extract their frequency-balanced power spectral intensities. Then, a machine learning model is applied to classify and recognize heart sound signals by combining the cepstrum coefficients of Mel and Gamma frequencies. The experiments are validated using the Yaseen public dataset with the 2016 PhysioNet/CinC Challenge dataset. The ten-fold cross-validation results show that the proposed effective feature vector combined with the K nearest neighbor classifier has an accuracy of up to 98.30% on the five-classified Yaseen dataset and 90% on the two-classified 2016 dataset. It can provide an effective reference for the clinical prevention and diagnosis of cardiovascular diseases.

articleTitle: 3D Object Detection for LiDAR Based on Improved PV-RCNN
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Addressing the current issue of poor performance in detecting small targets by lidar-based 3D object detection algorithms that combine point and voxel data, this paper proposes an improved PV-RCNN object detection algorithm named CBAM-RCNN. This algorithm introduces the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) to refine the Bird's Eye View (BEV) features after voxel compression. It assigns attention weights to the channel and spatial dimensions of the feature maps to enhance the expressive power of the features and subsequently improve the model's detection accuracy for small targets. Experiments on the KITTI dataset demonstrate that CBAM-RCNN achieves a 3.32% and 1.74% increase in mean Average Precision (mAP) for pedestrians and cyclists, respectively, compared to the baseline algorithm, verifying its effectiveness. Compared to current mainstream 3D object detection algorithms, CBAM-RCNN still exhibits better detection performance, further validating its advancement.

articleTitle: Lightweight Model for Rice Crop Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Rice is a staple crop for more than half of the world's population, making its health and yield crucial for global food security. Early detection of rice crop diseases can significantly mitigate yield losses and reduce the use of chemical treatments. In this paper, we propose a lightweight deep learning model designed for the efficient detection of rice crop diseases. The model leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) optimized for mobile and edge devices, ensuring that farmers in remote or resource-constrained areas can benefit from real-time disease detection. We demonstrate that our model achieves competitive accuracy with significantly reduced computational complexity compared to traditional models, making it an ideal solution for on- field deployment.

articleTitle: A Swin Transformer-Based model for smoke detection
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In order to minimize the damage caused by fire, it is especially important to detect smoke at the early stage of fire or when it is only produced. In this paper, we design a smoke detection network model SwinFP-Net based on the transformer algorithm, which enhances the global receptive field and reduces the arithmetic overhead through the sliding-window attention mechanism , in addition to using the feature pyramid structure to improve the detection accuracy of small targets. Validated by public dataset , the average precision of the proposed model for smoke detection is 88.5%.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Performance Optimization for Mobile Portal Service Gateway
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This research analyzes the performance loss caused by the service gateway of enterprise mobile portal to the H5 micro-apps it carries. Based on whether sensitive data is included, H5 micro applications are divided into two types. For H5 micro-apps that contain sensitive data, a service gateway performance optimization scheme is proposed. For H5 micro-apps that do not contain sensitive data, a lightweight service gateway is designed, which achieves overall performance improvement of the mobile portal service gateway.

articleTitle: Improved DeepCross AttentionNet for Recommendation Systems via Semantic Feature Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The Deep & Cross Network (DCN) and its derivative models have become important paradigms for click-through rate (CTR) prediction due to their efficient and superior performance. CTR prediction is one of the core tasks in recommendation systems, as it directly impacts users' interest and engagement with recommended content. Existing DCN models rely on explicit feature interaction methods, which heavily depend on feature quality. However, in prediction tasks with low-quality features, especially those with large amounts of sparse input, these interactions often introduce significant noise and may not be efficient in learning all types of feature crosses.This paper proposes an improved Deep Cross Network, named DeepCross AttentionNet (DCAnet), which retains the advantages of the DCN model while introducing a novel attention-based cross network designed to more effectively learn specific feature interactions. In particular, DeepCross AttentionNet (DCAnet) enhances the representation of sparse features through semantic feature [3] transformation. By converting sparse features into more informative semantic features, this approach not only enables the model to more accurately capture complex feature relationships but also significantly improves the accuracy of CTR prediction. We evaluated the CTR model in practical applications for recommendation systems, and the experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms many competitive models in our real-world recommendation system.

articleTitle: RSSI centre-of-mass localisation algorithm based on proposed Newton and median filtering
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: To address the problem that the Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) is subject to interference from the environment and other sources, causing errors in the received data,thus decreasing the positioning accuracy. In this document, an algorithm is proposed, which is an RSSI-weighted centre of mass location method based on Newton filtering and proposed median, RSSI data were optimised using Newton's method to improve accuracy. Median filtering was then performed to remove overlapping or erroneous information to ensure data quality. After experimental verification, the RSSI-weighted centre-of-mass localisation algorithm based on Newton and median filters performs excellently in terms of localisation accuracy, with an error reduction of 51.26% and 38.91% compared to the RSSI-based centre-of-mass localisation algorithm and RSSI-based weighted centre-of-mass localisation algorithm, respectively. This result gives us confidence in the performance and effectiveness of this algorithm and brings new possibilities for the development of positioning technology.

articleTitle: Adaptive beamforming algorithm for subarrays based on coprime array
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive beamforming algorithm based on the subarray technology of coprime array to avoid the occurrence of grating lobes and reduce complexity, in response to the problem of excessive data and computational complexity in processing large array antennas. Firstly, this paper divides the number of subarrays based on the number of elements in the coprime array; Subsequently, weighted compensation is performed within the subarray to compensate for the delay of the internal elements relative to the reference elements; Finally, subarray weighting is performed to enhance the output performance of the sampled signals. Compared with previous works, the proposed algorithm greatly reduces the computational complexity while improving the output performance of the adaptive beamformer at high signal-to-noise ratio. The validity and reliability of the proposed algorithm is verified through simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Data Flow Anomaly Detection based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The sophistication and diversity of contemporary cyberattacks have rendered the use of proxies, gateways, firewalls, and encrypted tunnels as a standalone defensive strategy inadequate. Consequently, the proactive identification of data anomalies has emerged as a prominent area of research within the field of data security. The majority of extant studies concentrate on sample equilibrium data, with the consequence that the detection effect is not optimal in the context of unbalanced data. In this study, the unsupervised learning method is employed to identify anomalies in dynamic data flows. Initially, multi-dimensional features are extracted from real-time data, and a clustering algorithm is utilised to analyse the patterns of the data. This enables the potential outliers to be automatically identified. By clustering similar data, the model is able to detect data behaviour that deviates significantly from normal traffic without the need for labelled data. The results of the experiments demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits high accuracy in the detection of anomalies across a range of scenarios. Notably, it demonstrates robust and adaptable performance, particularly in the context of unbalanced data.

articleTitle: Fake target Recognition Based on AIS Signal Propagation Attenuation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: AIS has become an important information system to ensure the safety of ship navigation. Then malicious users could use the openness and non-encryption of the protocol to generate fake targets into the AIS system, which poses a threat to the safety of ship navigation. For the AIS fake target threat, a recognition model based on AIS signal propagation attenuation is proposed. The feasibility of this method is verified by simulation, and the AIS fake target recognition is realized quickly and accurately.

articleTitle: Lightweight Channel Estimation Method for Dynamic OFDM System Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper presents a lightweight channel estimation technique for Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) systems based on deep learning. At the heart of the method is a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) that integrates a Multi-Scale Large Kernel Convolution (MLKC) module and a Convolutional Gating (CG) unit. The MLKC module, utilizing diverse large kernel sizes and a residual architecture, adeptly captures multi-scale features, enhancing the model's responsiveness to dynamic channel conditions. The CG unit optimizes the feature aggregation process through a spatial attention mechanism, improving the model's discernment of salient features. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms existing approaches across various channel environments, while maintaining a lower count of learnable parameters, showcasing a dual advantage of high efficiency and superior performance.

articleTitle: LHPF: An LLM-Based Hierarchical Pipeline Framework for Spoken Language Understanding
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In this study, we propose a hierarchical task learning framework based on Large Language Models (LLMs) to improve the performance in spoken language understanding (SLU). Our approach introduces an Alternative Entity Extract Model designed to assist LLMs in accurately extracting entities and locations from natural language utterances. Additionally, we develop an LLM-Based Hierarchical Pipeline Framework that integrates a small-scale model and an LLM in a pipeline, where the small model generates intermediate results, and the LLM refines the final output through prompts and intermediate results. By fine-tuning the LLM efficiently, we adapt it to downstream tasks, ensuring better generalization across both single-domain and cross-domain scenarios. Extensive experiments and quantitative analysis demonstrate that our proposed method not only excels in single-domain SLU tasks but also achieves robust performance in cross-domain settings. We achieve unification of the models on both single-domain and cross-domain problems

articleTitle: Integrated Design of Image Processing and Flight Control Based on AMP Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The ongoing development of intelligent ammunition has resulted in an expansion of the functions that such ammunition must perform, thereby increasing the demand for internal computing capabilities in both scale and complexity. In light of the diverse functional requirements, traditional single-processor architectures are inadequate to address the needs of these varied and complex tasks. Consequently, this article presents an integrated image processing and flight control technology based on an Asynchronous Multi-Processor (AMP) architecture. This approach consolidates two tasks with distinct requirements into a single module, effectively addressing the challenges associated with information exchange between tasks. The feasibility of this method has been validated through simulation testing.

articleTitle: Optimal Depth-of-Field Selection Method for Large Aperture Sonar Focusing Beamforming Based on Image Sharpness Function
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: When the large aperture horizontal array is used for underwater acoustic passive positioning, focus beamforming is carried out. At this time, the depth of field is divided into several levels according to a certain gain attenuation coverage (such as 3dB), and these depths of field are processed simultaneously, so that the global target information can be quickly mastered. However, due to the gain loss, azimuth deviation and even split results of a certain range target in different depth of field processing, it is easy to cause false alarm or omission of the target, increasing the difficulty of detection. This paper proposes an optimal depth of field selection method based on sharpness function, which can obtain the optimal depth of field for single or multiple targets or moving targets, and effectively improve the detection ability and detection efficiency.

articleTitle: Ternary Memory Composed of Ferroelectric Field-Effect Transistor Based on Dynamic Logic
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Ternary Content Addressable Memory (TCAM) is widely used in development areas such as network routers and machine learning, which are receiving significant attention. Ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) are among the most promising devices currently being researched in the field of advanced complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor (CMOS) technology. FeFETs also possess a unique hysteresis in the I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf>-V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf> characteristics, which allows the device to function as both a switch and a non-volatile (NV) memory element. Traditional TCAM has the problems of VTH drop or search disturbance. We leverage FeFET property to construct a novel TCAM based on dynamic logic that can be integrated as efficient and compact logic elements into various levels of the memory hierarchy. Due to the slow trend of performance scaling based on Moore's Law and the fact that many computational tasks are now more data-centric than compute-centric, it is highly necessary to design efficient and compact logic elements based on emerging technologies to enhance performance and conserve energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Quadratic Optimization Algorithm Based on Multi-array Fusion Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In this paper, we study related algorithms for multi-node localization in acoustic detection, and propose several data fusion methods in terms of multi-array fusion algorithms. A Monte Carlo simulation of the localization error under different fusion conditions is designed to derive the error model. Under the assumption of many arrays, we propose a weighted fusion method based on density clustering, and the simulation and experiments are made. The experimental results show that the multi-node data fusion positioning can effectively improve the positioning accuracy. on this basis, the optimization algorithm described in this paper has good positioning performance.

articleTitle: Design on Onboard Integrated Modular Intelligent Information System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Aimed at the information comprehensive development for satellite application service and resource collaboration, this paper proposes orderly center, mission center, and data center, to realize the functional fusion of satellite bus management, autonomous collaboration, and intelligent processing. Based on the SpaceVPX specification, universal Chassis profile and standardized hardware modules are implemented. Nine types of hardware modules, including Chassis basic service, network communication service and functional business service, are proposed and integrated to meet the carrying requirement of different applications. Propose three-plane integrated network design with high-reliability management plane, high-precision control plane, and high-bandwidth data plane, which horizontally bridging the end-to-end transmission barriers of the same plane network and vertically forming coverage different bandwidth zones.

articleTitle: Polarized light transmission in atmospheric aerosol consisting of mixed particle types
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Atmospheric aerosol is closely related to people’s daily life and scientific research activities, especially the frequent haze and dust weather in recent years, which has seriously affected social activities and scientific researches, for example, atmospheric communication. To overcome the shortcomings of traditional Monte Carlo algorithm of light scattering transmission, our study proposes a scattering medium model made of different atmospheric aerosol particles. Based on this model, Monte Carlo algorithm is improved and the polarized light transmission in atmospheric aerosol is simulated by incorporating T-matrix method. Through simulation experiments, the polarization characteristics of polarized light passing through the atmospheric aerosol made of different numbers and types of particles are studied. The results show that the polarization-preserving ability of circularly polarized light is obviously better than that of linearly polarized light, and different particle types and different proportion ratios have great influence on polarization-preserving ability. The medium model and the improved algorithm can help the theoretical analysis not only on the polarization imaging and target detection, but also on the free space optical communication under the realistic condition that the atmospheric aerosol exists.

articleTitle: Autonomous capability evaluation of UAV based on line graph method
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper proposed a line graph method to visually evaluate the autonomous capability of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). Firstly, the evaluation system of the UAV autonomous capability (UAV-AC) is constructed based on observe orient decide act (OODA) operational command theory. Secondly, the G1 method is proposed to calculate the index weights, which can objectively reflect the importance of each index and the subjective wishes of decision makers. Finally, the line chart method is used to display the autonomous capability of UAV, which provides a scientific and feasible technical means for evaluating the autonomous capability of UAV.

articleTitle: In-vehicle Noise Cancellation Based on Probabilistic Recognition Switching Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The functionality of modern vehicles is becoming increasingly comprehensive, with electronic equipment configurations growing more complex. However, operating screens and other devices while the driver's hands are off the steering wheel undoubtedly poses safety risks. Installing precise human-machine interaction devices can address this issue. Nevertheless, the presence of various types of in-car noise diminishes the accuracy of speech recognition. Hence, speech enhancement technology in the automotive environment is crucial. To address the issue of various mid-to-low-frequency noises such as engine and ground friction affecting speech recognition and communication, this study has designed a combined architecture of bimodal probabilistic Wiener filtering and bimodal probabilistic spectral subtraction algorithms. The prior signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) serves as the switching criterion; when the prior SNR is less than 0.35, a Wiener filter is utilized, and when it exceeds 0.35, a subtraction filter is employed to minimize the "musical noise" left by spectral subtraction. The conditional probabilities in the switching framework are derived from Bayes' theorem to identify constructive and destructive noises. The final simulation results demonstrate that compared to various traditional algorithms, the proposed combined architecture achieves the optimal performance in removing in-car noise and enhancing speech quality.

articleTitle: Classification of Pothole Laser Images Based on the Improved ResNet18 Network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper improves the pothole laser image classification model based on the ResNet18 network through transfer learning and the introduction of the SE channel attention mechanism. The study utilizes a self-made road inspection vehicle to collect a laser image dataset of road surfaces, which is then cropped and labeled. Experiments show that the improved SEResNet18 model outperforms the original ResNet18 and other mainstream networks in terms of classification accuracy and loss values, verifying the effectiveness of the SE module in enhancing classification performance. The research aims to improve the accuracy of pothole detection and provide technical support for road maintenance.

articleTitle: A Spectral Clustering-Based Pilot Assignment Method for Cell-Free Massive MIMO
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper studies pilot assignment (PA) in cell-free (CF) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO). PA is a key issue to facilitate signal processing, e.g. beamforming, by providing reliable channel estimation at access points (APs). Most existing methods face intractable local optima problem, which degrades the channel estimation accuracy. Moreover, these methods usually encounter the unaffordable complexity. To this end, we propose a low-complexity PA method based on the spectral clustering (SC), which is named as SC-based PA method. SC is a popular machine learning method for clustering problem in image segmentation, bioinformatics, etc. It leverages the eigenvectors of a similarity matrix to map the data samples to a low-dimensional space for easy clustering. By assigning the orthogonal pilot sequences to the same-cluster user equipments (UEs), the proposed SC-based PA method properly degrades the pilot contamination between the UEs. To verify the performance of the proposed method, we show by simulations that the proposed SC-based PA method outperforms the existing methods in both channel estimation accuracy and execution time.

articleTitle: Design of a Highly Integrated Ka-Band Phased Array Antenna-in-Package (AiP)
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: To address the issues of high connector loss and low system integration between the traditional active phased array antenna and the T/R modules, this paper designs a broadband integrated phased array antenna-in-package (AiP) module. Leveraging the advantages of Low-Temperature Co-fired Ceramic (LTCC) substrates, which offer strong multilayer wiring capabilities and the ability to form complex cavity structures, the antenna array and T/R modules are highly integrated. The chip stacking layout further enhances substrate utilization and improves the overall integration of the components. The AiP module operates within a bandwidth of 27.5-31 GHz, includes a 2×2 antenna array, and has dimensions of 10mm×10mm×5mm. Simulation results show that the receive link gain is greater than 25 dB, and the input/output voltage standing wave ratio (VSWR) is less than 1.65, demonstrating excellent electrical performance.

articleTitle: A Leakage Signal Identification Method Based on EEMD and Frequency Band Energy Ratios
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Infrasound-based pipeline leak detection represents a highly precise and versatile method. However, practical applications in long-distance gas pipelines face challenges due to the presence of operational noise, which often masks the faint infrasound signals generated by leaks. To tackle this issue, this study adopts Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) to process the non-stationary infrasound signals associated with leaks. Subsequently, leveraging the distinct autocorrelation characteristics between leak and noise signals, the signal is reconstructed to determine the leak presence based on energy distribution within the reference frequency band. Analysis of field data reveals significant disparities in frequency band energy distribution between leak and noise signals in the infrasound range, thereby enhancing the accuracy of leak detection. This approach provides pivotal insights for advancing infrasound-based leak detection systems.

articleTitle: Advanced Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Stage Bird Song Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Birdsong classification is vital for ecological monitoring, particularly in island wetlands. This study introduces the Multi-Stage (MS) model to address complex and mixed birdsong signals, comparing its performance against ResNet50, GoogLeNet Inception v1, and GoogLeNet Inception v4. Using a self-tested dataset of six bird species, the MS model achieved the highest recognition rate of 95.17%. The findings confirm the effectiveness of deep learning in birdsong recognition, while also highlighting the strengths and limitations of various models for specific tasks.

articleTitle: A Robust Multi-Channel InSAR Phase Unwrapping Method Based on Grouped Chinese Remainder Theorem
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In interferometric synthetic aperture radar (InSAR) multichannel system, multiple interferograms are obtained in multifrequency or multibaseline configuration, and can be used to reconstruct terrain height profiles. In this paper, a new robust method based on the modulus grouping Chinese remainder theorem (CRT) is proposed to solve the height reconstruction problem. This method uses modulus grouping and solves the estimated values of all target values when the error is integer 1 by compensating the remainder of the congruence equations of multiple congruence equations. The intersection of multiple sets of estimated values is solved, and the intersection is taken as the reconstructed elevation value. Compared with the existing robust CRT algorithm, the residual noise bound size of elevation reconstruction is extended from M / 4 to M, where M is the greatest common divisor of modulus. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: A high PSRR LDO design with Cascode compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: PSRR is an important measure for LDO circuits. For the conventional form of EA is improved by using cascode compensation, this method significantly improves the power supply rejection ratio (PSRR). The design is based on Eastern High-Tech's 0.18 μm BCD process and simulated with Cadence. The results show that the output voltage can be stabilized at 1.5 V when the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ref</inf> of the designed bandgap reference is 1.203 V. The load-adjustment ratio is 0.45%, the linearity-adjustment ratio is 0.6%, and the PSRR reaches -97 dB at low frequencies.

articleTitle: A U-Net-Based Deep Learning Method for R-Wave Detection in Wearable Device
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In the presence of noise or abnormal cardiac waveforms, achieving accurate QRS localization and heart rate estimation remains challenging, particularly when the ECG signals are acquired by wearable dynamic ECG monitoring devices. To address this issue, we propose a deep learning model based on the U-Net architecture. This method aims to improve the accuracy of R-wave detection, especially under conditions of noise or waveform abnormalities. The model was trained and validated using the the China Physiological Signal Challenge (CPSC) 2019 database, and its performance was further evaluated on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm achieved a heart rate calculation accuracy of 0.9421 on the CPSC 2019 non-public test set, and reached a sensitivity of 99.88% and a positive predictive value of 99.90% on the MIT-BIH database. The cross-database tests showed high accuracy and robustness, making it suitable for wearable device applications.

articleTitle: A 50 MHz BW 76.2 dB SNDR CT Modulator for Wireless Receiver
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In wireless communication systems, wideband analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) have consistently been a target and hotpots of research breakthroughs. Continuous-time sigma-delta ADCs employ oversampling noise-shaping techniques, along with their inherent anti-aliasing filtering capabilities, to achieve high-precision wideband analog-to-digital conversion, offering advantages in terms of speed, accuracy, and integration. This article presents a continuous-time sigma-delta modulator implemented with a 4th-order, 4-bit quantization feedback architecture, achieving a sampling rate of 2GHz and a signal bandwidth of 50 MHz. By embedding the resonator within the modulator loop, the in-band signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is improved. Additionally, a two-stage feedforward amplifier structure is designed to achieve higher energy efficiency. Under a supply voltage of 1.2V, simulation results demonstrate that the modulator achieves an SNDR of 76.2 dB, with a modulator loop power consumption of 78.4 mW.

articleTitle: Research on Group-level Pruning Algorithm Based on Progressive Sparsity Regularization
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of autonomous driving systems, deep learning models play a crucial role in their implementation. However, these models typically have high computational complexity and storage demands, posing challenges to the real-time processing capabilities of embedded devices. To address this issue, this paper proposes a group-level pruning algorithm based on progressive sparsity regularization. The algorithm groups model parameters and progressively increases the sparsity regularization strength, effectively reducing computational load and storage requirements while maintaining model performance. Additionally, the algorithm introduces group-level weight importance calculation based on the L2-norm, combined with weight gradient direction information to achieve a more refined pruning strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves a 2.58× speedup on the ResNet-56 model on the CIFAR dataset, significantly compressing the model's parameter size while maintaining accuracy. This research provides an effective solution for real-time applications such as autonomous driving, where efficient model deployment is essential.

articleTitle: Discussion on Stability Engineering Criterion of Negative Feedback Amplifier Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The stability criterion of amplifier circuit in analog circuit teaching, as a key knowledge point, is an important part of the knowledge system from "device to single-stage amplification (SSA) to multi-stage amplification (MSA) to integrated amplification to feedback". Most existing textbooks explain stability conditions based on the absence of self-excited oscillations, and the engineering criterion for the stability of negative feedback amplifier circuits is often presented without a thorough analysis of its conditions and applicability. This approach may lead to an inadequate understanding among students, hindering the development of skills that integrate engineering practice with theoretical knowledge. To address this issue, this paper first discusses the definition, analytical principles, and methods of stability in negative feedback amplification circuits. Subsequently, from the perspectives of "double-pole conditions" and "multi-pole conditions," it thoroughly analyzes and derives engineering criterion, and verifies its applicability. Introducing such applicability analysis effectively enhances students' understanding of the stability of negative feedback amplification circuits, which holds significant educational value.

articleTitle: An Efficient Overlap-Free Karatsuba Finite-Field Multiplier on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Finite field multipliers are widely used in various cryptography and coding system circuits. Due to their high complexity, the design quality of the multiplier determines the complexity and cost of the entire system. In order to reduce the complexity and cost of the multiplier, this paper proposes a finite field multiplier based on Overlap-free Karatsuba Algorithm (OKA). First, we analyze the theoretical number of gates and delays required for Schoolbook Multiplication Algorithm (SA), Karatsuba Algorithm (KA), and OKA. Then, we analyze the process of implementing the M-term KA algorithm when M is 3, 4, and 5. Next, we derive the Overlap-free Karatsuba Algorithm for M = 3, and use the three methods of SA, OKA2, and OKA3 for multi-level composition to implement an efficient multiplier (HA). Finally, we perform theoretical analysis and FPGA implementation on operands of 93-bit, 233-bit, and 409-bit. Our device utilization and delay indicate that the proposed HA multiplier is 20% faster than the SA multiplier, 34% faster than the standard KA multiplier, and 24% faster than the standard OKA multiplier, when compared in terms of the area-delay product (ADP). Compared with other multipliers in the literature, the proposed multiplier performs well in ADP performance evaluation.

articleTitle: WL distribution modeling of X-band small grazing Angle sea clutter via IPSO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In order to improve the heavy-tailed phenomenon in sea clutter modeling, the WL distribution modeling method and its statistical characteristics are studied. The IPSO (Improved Particle Swarm Optimization ) algorithm is used to estimate the sea clutter modeling parameters that obey the WL distribution, so as to improve the fitting effect of the statistical distribution model on sea clutter data. Based on the measured data of X-band sea clutter, the fitting effect of WL distribution on the measured data of sea clutter under different sea conditions is analyzed. Through the comparison with the goodness of fit test of statistical distribution models such as Rayleigh distribution, Weibull distribution, lognormal distribution and K distribution, it is shown that the WL distribution can well fit the sea clutter data with heavy tailing phenomenon, and has better statistical modeling ability of sea clutter amplitude distribution.

articleTitle: Research and Application on Special Packs Cigarettes Enter and Leave the Warehouse Automatically
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: With the change of market demand, special packs cigarettes show a rapid growth trend. At the same time, due to the diversity of its dimensions, it brings some challenges to the automatic storage of special packs cigarettes. Based on the actual production demand of Changde cigarette factory, this paper researches and designs a set of automatic storage solution of special packs cigarettes, and implements the verification in Changde cigarette factory, which has certain reference significance.

articleTitle: Two-ticket System Optimization for Power Grid Enterprise Safety Production based on Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Blockchain technology has demonstrated significant potential for application across various industries due to its unique characteristics of decentralization, tamper-proof security, and traceability. A blockchain-based power grid two-ticket system not only enhances the efficiency and security of grid management but also helps foster a more open, transparent, and efficient electricity market environment. As blockchain technology continues to mature and relevant laws and regulations evolve, its applications within the power grid two-ticket system are becoming more widespread, providing robust support for the development of the power grid. The advantages of this system are notable, with its decentralized architecture ensuring the security and immutability of two-ticket data, thereby reducing the cost of trust. The aim of this paper is to discuss the architectural design of a blockchain-based two-ticket system and explore how the characteristics of blockchain technology can improve the security, transparency, and efficiency of power grid operations and maintenance.

articleTitle: Towards Noise-Robust Partial Multi-Label Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In many real-world scenarios, acquiring accurate label information for multi-label data is challenging, often resulting in only partial label availability. This issue defines the partial multi-label learning problem (PML), primarily complicated by significant label noise (false-positive labels). This noise introduces two novel challenges: feature-label mismatch and inaccurate label correlation. To address these issues, we introduce a new noise-robust approach for PML, termed NRPML. NRPML employs non-negative matrix factorization (NMF) to learn low-dimensional latent features and label embeddings, effectively reducing false positives and noisy features. Additionally, an orthogonal constraint on the latent label embeddings enhances local label correlation, while a linear mapping based on these embeddings facilitates final predictions. Extensive comparative experiments in both traditional and partial multi-label learning scenarios demonstrate that NRPML outperforms existing state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Synchronization Analysis of Directed Complex Networks with Multi-Weights via Intermittent Control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This thesis analyses the synchronization issue for directed complex networks with multi-weights (CNMs). In the synchronization control scheme, the control strategy adopts non-periodically intermittent and pinning control methods, and the number of pinned nodes can be different in different sub-networks(coupling forms). Based on the Lyapunov stability theory, a linear feedback controller is designed, some sufficient conditions are derived for guaranteeing exponential synchronization of directed CNMs via intermittent control. Furthermore, two numerical simulations further validate the obtained conclusions.

articleTitle: Object Detection Methods for Autonomous Driving in Adverse Weather Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Autonomous driving systems open up a new frontier in the automotive industry, offering new possibilities for future transportation with increased efficiency and a comfortable experience. However, object detection in adverse weather conditions remains a challenge that hinders the advancement of higher-level autonomous driving. This paper provides a detailed report on the latest developments in target detection algorithms under adverse weather conditions. It analyzes the impact of adverse weather on autonomous vehicle sensors, the establishment and use of related datasets, research on image restoration algorithms for adverse weather conditions and their effects on target detection tasks, and the application of domain adaptation methods in transfer learning for target detection. Additionally, the paper discusses future work and potential research areas in this field.

articleTitle: Design and realization of assisted sleep detection system based on Internet of Things technology
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Sleep quality has a direct impact on an individual's life, working condition and health. However, professional sleep monitoring devices widely used on the market and in the medical field are expensive and complicated to operate, which can hardly meet the needs of individuals for long-term and convenient sleep monitoring. In view of this, this paper designs an affordable and user-friendly sleep monitoring system that focuses on capturing environmental factors affecting sleep in order to improve overall sleep quality. The system uses STM32 as the core control unit and works with the JDY31 Bluetooth module to transmit the collected information to the microcontroller through multiple sensors to monitor key indicators such as temperature, humidity, noise level, and human heart rate in the room in real-time and dynamically. After testing, the system can meet people's daily needs for sleep quality, successfully realizes data monitoring and visualization, and provides an effective tool for improving the sleep environment.

articleTitle: Water column detection method based on Doppler modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for the automatic detection of water columns in the presence of sea clutter, with the objective of facilitating the identification of water column targets. Firstly, a motion model of the water column target is established in accordance with the characteristics of the water column target. Subsequently, simulations were conducted to assess the efficacy of water column target detection at varying distances within the context of sea clutter. The simulated water column target was subjected to echo signal modulation and pulse compression, enabling the extraction of target Doppler frequency shift information. Subsequently, the Fast Fourier Transform is employed to analyse the Doppler information of the water column target in terms of amplitude-frequency, thereby constructing amplitude-frequency diagrams. Ultimately, the amplitude-frequency diagrams are inputted into the convolutional neural network for training, with the objective of obtaining the feature information of the water column target and optimising the network parameters through iteration, thus completing the water column target detection process. The network parameters are optimized in order to complete the detection of water column targets.

articleTitle: Ship Target Detection Using Distributed CFAR Detector with Multi-Radar System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Considering the great value of ship target detection and the outstanding detection performance with the multi-radar system, we apply a multi-radar distributed constant false alarm rate (CFAR) detector based on the local test statistic (LTS) to address the ship target detection issue. As the prerequisite for applying the distributed detector, we design a joint search scenario. To achieve the spatial diversity gain produced by the multi-radar system, we proposed a SNR-exponentially-weighted (SEW) approach to fuse the LTSs that use an exponential function to calculate the weights assigned to the LTSs according to their signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) values. Numerical results show that, with an appropriate sensitivity parameter, the SEW fusion is sufficient for nearly optimum performance and outperforms the unweighted sum fusion, especially when some radars have SNRs that are moderate but obviously higher compared to other radars.

Author Keywords: distributed detection based on local test statistic

articleTitle: Research on the Organization and Application of Shortwave Radio Stations under Extreme Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Shortwave radio stations, with their unique propagation characteristics, can still meet certain communication needs under extreme conditions such as blizzards and nuclear explosions. This paper explores the organization and application of shortwave radio stations in extreme conditions, focusing on the mechanisms of sky wave and ground wave propagation. It studies the impact of power, frequency, and signal-to-noise ratio on communication quality, while analyzing the effects of extreme conditions on the equipment itself and summarizing relevant conclusions to provide references for the organization and application of shortwave radio stations in extreme conditions.

articleTitle: Online Active Learning for Evolving Data Streams with Limited Labels
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The classification of data streams presents considerable challenges, especially in the context of concept drift and label scarcity. Many existing approaches struggle to efficiently classify data streams in the presence of concept drift, particularly when labeled data is scarce. This study proposes an innovative online active learning algorithm for data streams, referred to as OALEDS. The algorithm combines dynamic micro-clustering for concept representation with local class entropy modeling to effectively identify essential concepts and prototypes within continuously evolving data streams. Specifically, the algorithm places greater emphasis on prototypes in regions susceptible to concept drift, thereby concentrating on areas that reflect current data patterns. Additionally, a micro-clustering-based local class entropy strategy is employed to identify the most informative instances for labeling, optimizing the labeling process. Comprehensive experiments performed on both real-world and synthetic imbalanced datasets reveal that OALEDS efficiently adapts to concept drift, dynamically captures significant prototypes, and consistently surpasses state-of-the-art algorithms, even in scenarios with restricted labeling availability.

articleTitle: Probing the forced vibration of floaters and oscillators in a wave energy device in a single-degree-of-freedom system with different forms of damping coefficients
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In this paper, the heave motion of a floater and an oscillator in a wave energy device is investigated, and the forced vibration of a single-degree-of-freedom system under different damping coefficients is analyzed by mathematical modeling. Based on Newton's second law, the motions of the floater and oscillator are modeled and solved by the improved Runge-Kutta algorithm. By comparing the effects of two kinds of damping coefficients on the oscillatory characteristics of the system, this paper discusses the oscillatory behavior of the device in depth, and it is obtained that the difference in the form of damping does not affect the oscillatory characteristics of the system in a significant way. And the potential of the model in practical applications is verified.

articleTitle: Sleep staging method based on CEEMDAN-WPD algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: To solve the problem of the current sleep staging model's low accuracy, this study performed sleep stages by extracting multidimensional features after decomposing nocturnal respiratory signals. The acoustic signal was first preprocessed. The pre-processed signals are decomposed by complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) and wavelet packet decomposition (WPD), the Spearman correlation coefficients are calculated and appropriate thresholds are determined to retain the useful information components. The time-frequency domain and nonlinear features are extracted after reconstruction. Finally, it is fed into the classifier for sleep stage classification. A total of 7439 sleep acoustic signals were collected in the experiment. The experimental results show that the CEEMDAN-WPD algorithm proposed in this paper achieves an accuracy of 89.9% for REM/non-REM classification, and 84.3% for REM/light/deep sleep classification, effectively improving the classification accuracy compared with other methods.

Author Keywords: complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN)

articleTitle: A Fast Method for Transient Electromagnetic Scattering from a Ship on Rough Sea Surface
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: An efficient time-domain hybrid method combining time-domain integral equation (TDIE) and time-domain Kirchhoff approximation (TDKA) is proposed to calculate transient electromagnetic (EM) scattering of a 2D ship floating on a randomly rough sea surface under TM pulse wave incidence. In this hybrid method, the composite scattering model is divided into TDIE region and TDKA region. The TDIE region includes the ship and its adjacent sea surface, whereas the rest of the sea surface is designated as the TDKA region. The induced electric currents in the TDIE region and TDKA region are solved by TDIE and TDKA methods, respectively. To consider the coupling interactions between the TDIE region and the TDKA one, an iterative marching-on-in-time (MOT) based formulas are given and used to solve the transient scattering from a 2D ship on a sea surface. The accuracy and performance of the presented hybrid method are validated by comparing the backward scattered and specular scattered electric fields with those calculated by the full TDIE method. Numerical results show that the hybrid method of TDIE-TDKA can greatly reduce computational time with good calculation accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on transfer impedance calculation of high voltage shielded cables for electric vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: The high -voltage and high oscillating work characteristics of the high -voltage power line of electric vehicles have led to its serious electromagnetic compatibility problem. As a result, automakers have gradually adopted high -voltage cables with shielding layers. In the study of the shift impedance of the shielding layer, although the test method can test the size of its value more accurately, the cost is long and complicated. Therefore, this article mainly compares multiple coaxial cable woven layer transfer impedance calculation models, selects a computing model suitable for electric vehicle high -voltage shielding cables, and uses MATLAB for simulation. According to the comparison of the simulation value and the actual test results, it is proved to calculate the car shielding car shielding The scientific nature of the transfer impedance method of the line.

articleTitle: Traffic Sign Detection in Strong Glare Scenes
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: A traffic sign detection model based on image enhancement and the GD-YOLOv8 algorithm is proposed to address the issue of low detection accuracy of existing traffic sign detection models in strong glare scenes. For low-quality traffic sign images, histogram equalization is adopted to enhance overexposed image regions. To address the issues of missed detections and false alarms, a traffic sign detection model based on the GD-YOLOv8 algorithm is designed to fully extract traffic sign feature information. Experimental results on the GLARE dataset show that the proposed method achieves an average improvement of 12.31% in detection accuracy compared to SSD, Faster R-CNN, YOLOv5s, YOLOv7, and YOLOv8n, demonstrating its effectiveness in strong glare scenes.

articleTitle: Research and Development of Mining Wired Drilling Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Measurement while drilling (MWD) is a commonly used directional drilling technique that can measure the inclination angle, azimuth angle, tool face angle and other parameters of the borehole in real time and intuitively, making it easy for drilling personnel to monitor the drilling situation in real time. It can also adjust the inclination angle and process parameters of the drilling tool according to the design trajectory. The explosion-proof computer has been miniaturized, three commonly used measurement-while-drilling computers have been combined into one, and the transmission distance of the wired system has been increased. This article introduces the working principle of the underground wired drilling measurement system in coal mines. It elaborates on its composition and function from two parts: the measurement short section and the borehole computer. The system is tested and the results show that it meets the requirements of directional drilling.

articleTitle: Design of General Automated Test System for Integrated Guidance and Control Device
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: A universal automated testing system for integrated control devices has been developed to facilitate the automated testing and verification of these devices. This system encompasses the architecture of the testing framework as well as the design and implementation of the associated testing software. By simulating various on-board components that interact with the integrated guidance and control device, the system enables comprehensive functional testing and verification in accordance with the specified testing requirements. The results of the tests indicate that the system operates reliably and effectively meets the functional, performance, and reliability testing needs of diverse products. Consequently, this advancement enhances testing efficiency and fulfills the automation integration testing requirements for integrated control devices.

articleTitle: A new variable step-size hybrid affine projection algorithm for active noise control
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Impulsive noise is common in active noise control (ANC) applications. The hybrid affine projection algorithm (H-APA) has excellent performance in dealing with impulse noise outliers as compared to traditional ANC algorithms. Accordingly, this paper proposes H-FxAPA, which is derived from the application of H-APA to ANC. Based on the analysis of the steady state step size of H-FxAPA, a new variable step-size method of the algorithm is proposed, which is an extended application of the steady state analysis and adjusts the change of the step-size by an introduced control term, called as NVSS-H-FxAPA. Simulation demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed algorithms to cope with impulse noise and its superiority over similar state-of-the-art algorithms.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization of Communication Technology Based on Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Distributed deep learning systems commonly use synchronous data parallelism to train models. However, communication overhead can be costly in distributed environments with limited communication bandwidth. To reduce communication overhead, an intuitive approach is to increase the communication interval. However, increasing the communication interval often affects the convergence speed of the model, requiring more epochs to train the model to the target accuracy, thereby reducing the statistical efficiency of the training algorithm. To address these issues in distributed synchronous data parallel training algorithms and communication interval selection methods, this paper proposes a training algorithm that combines skip communication strategies and correction techniques to ensure low communication overhead and high statistical efficiency. The training algorithm maintains a small batch size through local updates in each training process and employs correction techniques to reduce the divergence among individual local models, thereby ensuring high statistical efficiency. At the same time, the training algorithm utilizes a skip communication strategy to update the global model, meaning that the global model is not updated with every iteration, but rather updated once every few iterations. This reduces the frequency of communication, ensuring low communication overhead. Experimental results show that this training algorithm reduces total training time by 88.9%, 74.9%, 34.1%, and 82.4% compared to SSGD, SkipSSGD, LocalSGD, and SMA, respectively.

articleTitle: Blind adaptive digital background calibration technology of offset in Time-Interleaved ADC
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a blind adaptive digital background calibration method designed to correct errors due to offsets between channels in time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (TI ADCs). By using the DC voltage of one ADC channel as a reference, the method calibrates the offset voltages of the other channels. This approach is notable for its lack of dependence on input signal information and its ability to adapt to variations in channel offsets. A 1 GHz, 12-bit dual-TI ADC is simulated using Simulink to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results demonstrate that, despite a 10% channel offset, significant performance improvements were achieved. The Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio (SNDR) increased from 29.4 dB to 68.1 dB, and the Effective Number of Bits (ENOB) improved from 4.59 bits to 11.01 bits. Furthermore, the calibration results remained stable and consistent across an offset range of 0% to 25%.

articleTitle: Short-term wind power forecasting model based on improved Tasmanian Devil algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of insufficient convergence speed and convergence accuracy of the prediction model caused by the variability and volatility of wind speed, a combined prediction model of SSA-VMD-ITDO-LSTM based on variational mode decomposition, improved Tasmanian devil optimization algorithm and long short-term memory network was proposed. Firstly, the SSA-VMD method is used to decompose the original wind speed series to obtain relatively stable wind speed sub-series, and the LSTM model is used to obtain the time correlation of the input data series. Then, the Brownian random walk strategy is used to update the population position and the stochastic center of gravity differential evolution strategy are used to optimize the global and improve the robustness to find the optimal solution. The parameters of the LSTM model are optimized with the improved Tasmanian devil optimization algorithm, and finally the final predicted value of wind power is obtained by superimposing the predicted value of each subsequences. The model is applied to the actual wind power prediction, and compared with other eight models, the experimental results show that the three average errors of the stroke power value of the model are the smallest, and the RMSE, MAE and MAPE values are 0.83367, 0.67062 and 1.5439%, respectively.

articleTitle: Extraction of vital signs from frequency modulated continuous wave radar based on moth-flame optimized successive variational mode decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: Vital signs are extracted from frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar devices, taking into account that respiratory and heartbeat signals are non-stationary and non-linear, as well as their susceptibility to interference from respiratory harmonics, intermodulation waves, and noise signals, and the issue of manually selecting the balancing parameter for the successive variational mode decomposition (SVMD). A vital signs extraction method based on moth flame optimization algorithm (MFO) optimizing SVMD and variance contribution rate (VCR) screening criteria is proposed. The method first preprocesses the radar raw echo signal by performing range dimension fast Fourier transform (FFT), static clutter filtering, selecting range cells through the maximum range gate, and processing the phase to obtain vital signs; then decomposes the vital sign using MFO-SVMD, optimizes the balancing parameters through MFO to avoid information loss and redundancy caused by unsuitable balancing parameters; subsequently filters out suitable modal components as respiratory and heartbeat signals using VCR; finally, extracts respiratory and heartbeat frequencies using FFT peak detection. Results of research indicate that the suggested approach can adaptively optimize the balancing parameter in SVMD and accurately extract respiratory and heartbeat information.

articleTitle: ELFGMNet object detection algorithm, improved based on EfficientDet network
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: To address challenges in detecting dense, occluded, and background-interfered targets, we propose a new detection network called the Efficient Local Filter with Gate Mechanism Detection Network, which improves upon EfficientDet. ELFGMNet enhances feature extraction by replacing simple attention mechanisms with a channel-sensitive mechanism that updates weights more effectively, improving multi-scale feature fusion and feature expression. Additionally, it introduces a lightweight multi-scale gate feature enhancement module for class/box processing, which adapts to interference and occlusion by learning to prioritize important features and suppress noise, thus boosting detection performance.On the VOC2007 dataset, ELFGMNet achieves a best mAP@0.5 of 83.31%, a 2.23% improvement over EfficientDet, and outperforms other advanced models.

Author Keywords: Multi-Scale Local Gate Feature Enhancement Network

articleTitle: Recording Shielding System Based on Ultrasonic Waves
publicationTitle: 2024 3rd International Conference on Electronics and Information Technology (EIT)
abstract: This system uses the STM32H750 microcontroller as its core to implement an ultrasonic-based blocking recording shielding system through a recording shielding signal generator and an audio signal monitoring and recognition module. It includes recording shielding and audio monitoring and recognition functions. The shielding range can be adjusted by modulating the output power. The microcontroller controls the amplitude and frequency of the output shielding signal by controlling the direct digital frequency synthesizer (DDS) module, which in turn adjusts the intensity of the emitted ultrasonic waves. After passing through a Class D amplifier, the shielding signal can drive the ultrasonic transducer to emit ultrasonic waves, thereby blocking audio signals to achieve the recording shielding effect. The system also converts audio signals into electrical signals that can be captured by the microcontroller's on-chip analog-to-digital converter (ADC) through a microphone module, low-pass filter, and DC bias circuit. It calculates the zero-crossing rate(ZCR) and spectral centroid(SC) of the acquired voltage array to determine whether there is an audio signal in the environment and to recognize the types of audio signals.The system also utilizes wavelet analysis and neural networks to improve the accuracy of monitoring and recognition.
